title: Weekly Regression Digest — Fail Mode Census 2026-03-12
body:
Purpose:
This is a concise, operational digest from applied-ml capturing the latest biweekly regression census across onboarding promptsets (snapshot window: 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-11). Goal is to list the dominant fail modes, highlight high-impact examples, and surface concrete action items with owners and fast timelines so we can reduce P0 regressions before the next hosted rollout.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Net quality delta (primary metric: weighted ROUGE-1 similarity against golden answers + safety filters): -3.1% vs baseline (model v2.17 -> v2.18 candidate).
- Top 3 fail modes by incident count: hallucination on knowledge cutoff edges (34%), instruction-skipping (22%), and hallucinated citations/URLs (14%).
- 8 promptsets exceed tolerance threshold (>5% failure rate); two are high-priority for customers (customer-facing agent and faq-bot).
- Short-term mitigations: targeted prompt repairs + sentinel tests in CI, canary rollback threshold lowered to 1.5% P0 regressions.

What we ran / dataset notes:
- Evaluation harness: onboarding-evals-v3 (see linked_confluence runbook).
- Promptsets included: faq-bot, agent-proactive, internal-kb-retrieval, code-synthesis-smoke, intl-zh-summary, commercial-terms, ecommerce-classify, finance-qa (total 42 promptsets, 12k eval items).
- Sampling: stratified by intent type + token-length quintiles.
- Golden answers: curated by solutions eng + QA with versioned promptset ids.

Census: fail mode breakdown (counts are absolute failure events across eval items):
1) Hallucination near knowledge cutoff (n=408, 34% of failures): outputs invent facts dated after cutoff or fabricate events. Example: prompt 'When did the Redwood Dedicated GA launch?' -> model replies 'September 2025' but golden = 'Feb 2024'. Note pattern concentrated in long-context prompts referencing recent dates.
2) Instruction-skipping / incomplete steps (n=264, 22%): model returns terse answer ignoring multi-step instruction (e.g., asked to produce numbered checklist, returns paragraph). Mostly observed in code-synthesis-smoke and agent-proactive promptsets.
3) Fabricated citations and URLs (n=168, 14%): model invents domain names or returns plausible-looking but incorrect DOI/URL strings.
4) Tokenization truncation leading to answer cutoffs (n=116, 9.5%): downstream post-processing dropped tail tokens; reproduces on longer inputs.
5) Safety fallback false positives (n=94, 7.8%): answers flagged as unsafe when they are benign — correlated with new moderation embeddings update.
6) Numeric precision drift (n=78, 6.5%): rounding or unit conversion mistakes in finance-qa promptset.
7) NLU misclassification in multiclass tasks (n=62, 5.2%): taxonomy mapping errors in ecommerce-classify.

Top failing promptsets (by failure rate and customer impact):
- faq-bot: 11.2% failure rate, high customer exposure (critical).
- agent-proactive: 9.5% failure rate, triggers automated emails -> potential brand risk.
- finance-qa: 7.8% failure rate, MSE impact on downstream scoring.
- code-synthesis-smoke: 6.4% failure rate, developer UX regressions.
- intl-zh-summary: 5.9% failure rate, concentrated on long-form summaries.

Representative failure snippets (redacted):
- Promptset: faq-bot | Prompt: 'When was the Dedicated product GA?' | Candidate: 'September 2025' | Golden: 'February 2024' | Notes: hallucination tied to presence of multiple date tokens in context.
- Promptset: code-synthesis-smoke | Prompt: 'Return a bash script to rotate logs and gzip older than 7 days.' | Candidate: '... tar -czf /var/log/oldlogs.tar.gz -mtime +7' | Golden: uses find + xargs; candidate missed -type f and has incorrect mtime usage.
- Promptset: intl-zh-summary | Candidate: dropped last sentence repeatedly for inputs > 1024 subword tokens.

Diagnostics we ran:
- Delta-heatmap: per-layer attention norm shift (v2.18 vs v2.17) shows 3x increase in cross-attn variance on tokens labeled as 'date' / 'doc-meta'. Implication: kernel selection changed for long contexts.
- Kernel/quantization config: v2.18 candidate uses int8-quant faster kernel on A100 pools in dedicated; correlated with truncation failures.
- Moderation embeddings: rolled new moderation model 2026-03-03; correlated with safety false positives.

Hypotheses (ranked by plausibility):
- H1 (high): quantization profile + new kernel combination reduces stability for long-context date tokens -> causes hallucination and truncation. Evidence: reproduces locally when switching to same kernel flags.
- H2 (medium): attention-weight pruning heuristic introduced in v2.18 biases early-decoder steps causing instruction-skipping.
- H3 (low): dataset drift in golden answers (some golds outdated) causing apparent hallucinations — partially true for 12 items but not majority.

Immediate actions (0-7 days):
- A1: Add targeted sentinel tests for faq-bot and agent-proactive to CI with focused date/place templates (owner: Diego Alvarez, ETA: 48h).
- A2: Rollback kernel selection to baseline for canary cohort if P0 regressions >1.5% (owner: Samir Patel, ETA: 24h to implement policy).
- A3: Hot prompt repair for finance-qa to enforce numeric format checks and unit assertions in template (owner: Priya Natarajan, ETA: 72h).
- A4: Re-run quantization ablation (int8 vs int16) on subset of long-context items to quantify effect size (owner: Aisha Kaur, ETA: 5 days).
- A5: Re-evaluate moderation embedding rollout for false positives; gate with threshold + allowlist for benign categories (owner: Security/Compliance contact: Jacob Reese, ETA: 7 days).

Medium term (2–6 weeks):
- M1: Implement attention-stability regression test that tracks cross-attn variance on labeled token classes across model builds. Integrate as dashboard alert.
- M2: Expand canary to 2% traffic with automated rollback if P0 regressions spike; include route-level isolation for customer-facing promptsets.
- M3: Schedule prompt tuning sweep (few-shot/context engineering) for faq-bot and agent-proactive to reduce hallucination risk.

Owners / responsibility matrix (short):
- Eval harness + CI sentinels: Diego Alvarez (applied-ml).
- Canary policy + infra flags: Samir Patel (serving-runtime infra).
- Promptset repairs & QA: Priya Natarajan (solutions-eng).
- Quantization ablation & kernel profiling: Aisha Kaur (applied-ml).
- Moderation gating: Jacob Reese (security).

Metrics to watch (dashboards/SLAs):
- P0 regression rate (per-model, per-promptset) — target <1.0% post-mitigation.
- Weighted ROUGE delta and fraction of hallucination events.
- Canary revert frequency and rollback latency.
- Customer-facing incidents (CS escalations) tied to promptsets.

Quick notes / decisions made in sync (2026-03-13 standup):
- Agreed to lower canary regression threshold to 1.5% for immediate build.
- Diego to push sentinel tests to ci-onboarding branch by EOD.
- Samir will open infra ticket to enable kernel pinning per-route (Linear: ML-1279).

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Can we automatically detect date-like hallucinations by heuristic and prefer conservative 'I don't know' or cite-sourcing? (action: research spike).
- Is the truncation issue purely downstream postprocessing or model-likelihood? Need token-level logging on canary.

Attachments / anchors:
- Linked Linear ticket: ML-1245 (fail-mode census)
- PR to models repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/493 (quant-flag experiments)
- Confluence runbook: confluence:Onboarding-eval-runbook

Appendix: quick reproduction steps (for engineers)
1) Checkout branch: models/quant-experiments/v2.18-local-repro.
2) Run: python eval/harness.py --promptset faq-bot --sample-size 1000 --kernel-override int8_fused --log-attention --out debug-faq-v2.18.json
3) Compare with baseline: python eval/compare.py --base debug-faq-v2.17.json --cand debug-faq-v2.18.json --metrics rouge1,hallucination_count

Notes to self (informal):
- Prioritize faq-bot because it's user-visible; keep customers in the loop if we plan a canary rollback.
- This digest is intentionally terse — will expand with charts in the dashboard export next update.

-- Aisha
